name: Update the active rolling release to the next stage for a project
description: Update the active rolling release to the next stage for a project Advance a rollout to the next stage. POST /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/approve-stage
context:
POST /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/approve-stage
Advance a rollout to the next stage. This is only needed when rolling releases is configured to require manual approval.
Required: idOrName (path) — Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)
Optional: teamId (query) — The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.; slug (query) — The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.; body (body)

name: Complete the rolling release for the project
description: Complete the rolling release for the project Force-complete a Rolling Release. POST /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/complete
context:
POST /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/complete
Force-complete a Rolling Release. The canary deployment will begin serving 100% of the traffic.
Required: idOrName (path) — Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)
Optional: teamId (query) — The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.; slug (query) — The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.; body (body)

name: Delete rolling release configuration
description: Delete rolling release configuration Disable Rolling Releases for a project means that future deployments will not undergo a rolling release. DELETE /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/config
context:
DELETE /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/config
Disable Rolling Releases for a project means that future deployments will not undergo a rolling release. Changing the config never alters a rollout that's already in-flight—it only affects the next production deployment. If you want to also stop the current rollout, call this endpoint to disable the feature, and then call either the /complete or /abort endpoint.
Required: idOrName (path) — Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)
Optional: teamId (query) — The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.; slug (query) — The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.

name: Get the active rolling release information for a project
description: Get the active rolling release information for a project Return the Rolling Release for a project, regardless of whether the rollout is active, aborted, or completed. GET /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release
context:
GET /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release
Return the Rolling Release for a project, regardless of whether the rollout is active, aborted, or completed. If the feature is enabled but no deployment has occurred yet, null will be returned.
Required: idOrName (path) — Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)
Optional: state (query) — Filter by rolling release state; teamId (query) — The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.; slug (query) — The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.

name: Get rolling release billing status
description: Get rolling release billing status Get the Rolling Releases billing status for a project. GET /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/billing
context:
GET /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/billing
Get the Rolling Releases billing status for a project. The team level billing status is used to determine if the project can be configured for rolling releases.
Required: idOrName (path) — Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)
Optional: teamId (query) — The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.; slug (query) — The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.

name: Get rolling release configuration
description: Get rolling release configuration Get the Rolling Releases configuration for a project. GET /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/config
context:
GET /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/config
Get the Rolling Releases configuration for a project. The project-level config is simply a template that will be used for any future rolling release, and not the configuration for any active rolling release.
Required: idOrName (path) — Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)
Optional: teamId (query) — The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.; slug (query) — The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.

name: Start a rolling release for the project
description: Start a rolling release for the project Start a rolling release for a deployment. POST /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/start
context:
POST /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/start
Start a rolling release for a deployment. If a rolling release is already active for the same canary deployment, returns the current state without side effects.
Required: idOrName (path) — Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)
Optional: teamId (query) — The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.; slug (query) — The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.; body (body)

name: Update the rolling release settings for the project
description: Update the rolling release settings for the project Update (or disable) Rolling Releases for a project. PATCH /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/config
context:
PATCH /v1/projects/{idOrName}/rolling-release/config
Update (or disable) Rolling Releases for a project. When disabling with the resolve-on-disable feature flag enabled, any active rolling release document is resolved using the disableRolloutAction parameter: "abort" to roll back (default), or "complete" to promote the canary to production. When enabling or updating config, changes only affect the next production deployment and do not alter a rollout that's already in-flight. Note: Enabling Rolling Releases automatically enables skew protection on the project with the default value if it wasn't configured already.
Required: idOrName (path) — Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)
Optional: teamId (query) — The Team identifier to perform the request on behalf of.; slug (query) — The Team slug to perform the request on behalf of.
